laws.penalty: Unjustified use of force: potential criminal charges and civil liability.
laws.exceptions: Force always subject to the reasonableness standard.

quiz.q: When may South Carolina officers use deadly force?
options: When reasonably necessary to prevent death or serious injury
quiz.explanation: South Carolina officers may use deadly force only when reasonably necessary to prevent death or serious injury.

laws.subtitle: S.C. Code Ann. §N/A — Extreme Risk Protection Orders
laws.fullDescription: South Carolina does not have a Red Flag (ERPO) law. No Red Flag law.
laws.penalty: N/A — ERPO is a civil court order, not a criminal penalty.

quiz.q: Does South Carolina have a Red Flag (ERPO) law?
quiz.explanation: South Carolina does not have an Extreme Risk Protection Order law.

laws.title: Hate Crime Laws
laws.subtitle: S.C. Code Ann. §Criminal Code — Bias-motivated crime laws
laws.fullDescription: South Carolina has hate crime sentencing enhancements.
laws.penalty: Hate crime enhancement or separate charge: sentencing enhancement.
laws.exceptions: Protected speech expressing bias without accompanying criminal conduct is constitutionally protected.

quiz.q: Does South Carolina have hate crime laws?
quiz.explanation: South Carolina: Hate crime enhancements apply.

laws.title: Domestic Violence Laws & Protections

laws.fullDescription: South Carolina: Comprehensive DV protections including protective orders.
laws.penalty: Violation of DV protective order: misdemeanor to felony..
laws.exceptions: Mutual protective orders may be issued in some circumstances.

quiz.q: Does South Carolina have mandatory arrest policies for domestic violence?
quiz.explanation: South Carolina: DV protective orders and protections available.

laws.title: Stalking & Cyberstalking Laws
laws.subtitle: S.C. Code Ann. §Criminal Code — Stalking prohibition
laws.fullDescription: South Carolina prohibits stalking — repeated non-consensual contact causing substantial distress. Stalking prohibited; cyberstalking covered.
laws.penalty: First-degree stalking: felony. Second-degree: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Lawful investigations by law enforcement are not considered stalking.

quiz.q: Is cyberstalking (electronic harassment) covered by South Carolina's stalking law?
quiz.explanation: South Carolina's stalking law covers cyberstalking through electronic means.

laws.fullDescription: South Carolina: Data breach notification required.
laws.penalty: Data breach notification: civil fines.
laws.exceptions: Small businesses may have reduced obligations under some state laws.

quiz.q: Does South Carolina have a comprehensive consumer data privacy law?
quiz.explanation: South Carolina: Breach notification rules only.

laws.title: Social Media Age Verification
laws.subtitle: S.C. Code Ann. §N/A — No state law

quiz.q: Does South Carolina require age verification for social media?

laws.title: Environmental Regulations
laws.subtitle: S.C. Code Ann. §Environmental Code — Environmental protection
laws.fullDescription: South Carolina: State env agency enforces air, water, waste rules.
laws.penalty: Environmental violations: civil fines up to $25000/day; criminal penalties for willful violations.
laws.exceptions: Some agricultural and industrial uses have specific permitting pathways.

quiz.q: Which agency enforces environmental laws in South Carolina?
quiz.explanation: South Carolina's state environmental agency works alongside the EPA to enforce environmental laws.

laws.fullDescription: South Carolina: South Carolina has a renewable portfolio standard for electric utilities.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a policy/utility requirement, not a criminal law.

quiz.q: Does South Carolina have a Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS)?

laws.penalty: Retailer violations: N/A.
laws.exceptions: Bags for meat, produce, or bulk items are often exempt.

quiz.q: Does South Carolina have a statewide plastic bag ban or fee?

quiz.q: Does South Carolina have a bottle deposit/redemption law?

laws.title: Animal Cruelty Laws
laws.subtitle: S.C. Code Ann. §Criminal Code — Animal cruelty prohibition
laws.fullDescription: South Carolina prohibits cruelty to animals including torture, beating, neglect, and fighting. Animal cruelty is a felony; neglect is a misdemeanor.
laws.penalty: Intentional cruelty: felony (up to 5 years). Neglect: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Lawful hunting, fishing, pest control, and veterinary procedures are exempt.

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for intentional animal cruelty in South Carolina?
quiz.explanation: South Carolina: Intentional animal cruelty is punishable by felony (up to 5 years).

laws.title: Exotic Pet Ownership
laws.subtitle: S.C. Code Ann. §Wildlife Code — Exotic and wild animal ownership
laws.fullDescription: South Carolina: Dangerous exotic animals generally prohibited as pets.
laws.penalty: Unlawful possession of prohibited animal: misdemeanor or felony; animal seizure..
laws.exceptions: Licensed zoos, wildlife rehabilitators, and research institutions may keep otherwise prohibited animals.

quiz.q: Are large exotic cats (lions, tigers) legal as pets in South Carolina?
quiz.explanation: South Carolina: Large exotic cats banned as pets.

laws.fullDescription: South Carolina: Consumer fireworks regulated.
laws.penalty: Fireworks violation: $500–$2000 fines plus liability for fire damage.
laws.exceptions: Licensed pyrotechnic operators may use professional-grade fireworks at permitted events.

quiz.q: Are consumer aerial fireworks legal in South Carolina?
quiz.explanation: South Carolina: Safe-and-sane fireworks allowed with local restrictions.

laws.title: Gambling Laws
laws.subtitle: S.C. Code Ann. §Gaming Code — Gambling regulations
laws.fullDescription: South Carolina: Commercial gambling is illegal in South Carolina. Video poker was illegal since 2000. A state lottery exists.
laws.penalty: Illegal gambling: Illegal gambling: misdemeanor..
laws.exceptions: Charitable gaming (bingo, pull tabs) for nonprofits typically permitted with license.

quiz.q: Are commercial casinos legal in South Carolina?
quiz.explanation: South Carolina: South Carolina has no commercial casinos; only a state lottery.
